question: Name the process that causes living cells to expand in size and shape when placed in a hypotonic solution.
solution:
The correct answer is __**Osmosis.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**Osmosis:

__
 
• It is the process by which solvent molecules move through a semi-permeable membrane from a solution of low concentration to one of high concentration.
 
• It is a passive process that takes place without using any energy.
 
• In a** hypotonic solution, a cell will gradually inflate and grow until it bursts.**
 
• It can occur in any solvent, including gases and supercritical liquids.
 
• It is of two types:
 
 
• Endosmosis: When a substance is dissolved in a hypotonic solution, the solvent molecules enter the cell and cause deplasmolysis or turgidness.
 
• Exosmosis: When a material is dissolved in a hypertonic solution, the solvent molecules leave the cell and cause plasmolysis or the cell to become floppy.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**Transpiration:

 
• It is the mechanism by which extra water is removed from the plant's body.
 
• It is typically the result of water evaporating off the leaf surface.
 
• Variables influencing the transpiration rate are sunlight, temperature, wind, and humidity.

**Photosynthesis:**

 
• It is the process by which plants convert **light energy into chemical energy.**
 
• It is essential for the** growth and survival of plants.**
 
• It releases **oxygen** as a byproduct.
 
• It is an **essential component** of the food chain.
